title: Processes, workers and scaling
summary: child_process, worker_threads and cluster, signals and exit codes, and when each tool fits.

sections.title: The process object
sections.body:
`process` describes the running program: `argv`, `env`, `cwd()`, `pid`, `memoryUsage()`, `exitCode`. It is also an emitter for signals (`SIGTERM`, `SIGINT`) and lifecycle events (`exit`, `beforeExit`, `unhandledRejection`).

Prefer setting `process.exitCode = 1` and letting the loop drain over calling `process.exit(1)`, which stops immediately and can cut off pending log writes.

sections.title: Child processes
sections.body: `child_process.spawn(cmd, args)` runs another program with streams for stdin, stdout and stderr; `execFile` collects the output for you. Avoid `exec` with user input: it runs through a shell, so `; rm -rf` in an argument becomes a command. Pass arguments as an array and do not enable `shell`.

sections.title: Worker threads
sections.body: `worker_threads` run JavaScript on extra threads, each with its own event loop and heap. Use them for CPU-bound work (image resizing, parsing, hashing) so the main loop keeps serving requests. They communicate with `postMessage`, which copies data via structured clone; `ArrayBuffer`s can be transferred and `SharedArrayBuffer`s shared. Keep a pool of workers instead of starting one per task.

sections.title: Scaling across cores
sections.body: One Node process uses one core for JavaScript. To use more, run several processes: the `cluster` module forks workers that share a listening port, or, more commonly today, run one process per container and let the orchestrator and load balancer scale them. Either way, keep processes **stateless**: sessions, caches and rate-limit counters that must be shared live in Redis or a database.

pitfalls: Passing user input to `exec` or `spawn` with `shell: true`.
Calling `process.exit()` while logs or responses are still being written.
Using worker threads for I/O-bound work that the event loop already handles.
Keeping per-process in-memory state that should be shared across instances.

gotchas.question: Worker threads or child processes?
gotchas.answer: Worker threads share one process, start faster and can share memory, so they suit CPU-heavy JavaScript. Child processes are fully isolated and can run any program, so they suit running other tools or untrusted, crash-prone work.

gotchas.question: What exit code does a process get when killed by SIGTERM?
gotchas.answer: Conventionally 128 + the signal number, so 143 for SIGTERM (15) and 130 for SIGINT (2). If you handle the signal yourself, you choose the code, usually 0 after a clean shutdown.

gotchas.question: Why can `cluster` break in-memory sessions?
gotchas.answer: Each worker is a separate process with its own memory. A login stored in worker A is unknown to worker B, so the next request may appear logged out. Store sessions externally or use stateless tokens.
